method: Live HTTP probing (curl + node) against leverarms.com. NO DB writes. 800ms inter-request delay. Side-by-side comparison of R1 candidate vs DB siteProfile.
verdict: R1 candidate is correct on every load-bearing field. The DB siteProfile contains stale/legacy residue that should NOT be propagated. Two DB-side errors flagged for correction.

corrections.reasoning: Re-ran heavy 8-batch WAF probe. Cloudflare passive (cf-ray + __cf_bm on every response). Rapid 10x burst all 200. Crawler paths (/, /product-category/*, /wp-json/wc/store/v1/*) all 200. SQLi/XSS payloads + honeypots (xmlrpc.php, .env, .git/config, wp-config.php) return 403 with body 'nginx 403 Forbidden' — origin-side rules, NOT a Cloudflare challenge. No bot-UA blocking (python-requests/2.28 -> 200). No sucuri headers anywhere. No plugin-WAF body markers. Per SKILL.md operational rule, rule-selective Cloudflare on attack payloads only != WAF blocking the crawler. R1's hasWaf=false is correct. DB row is internally inconsistent (hasWaf=true + wafType=cloudflare-passive + needsPlaywright=false) — residue from a previous misclassification (DB notes flagged a prior 'sucuri' tag).
Both agree. Re-probe confirms cloudflare-passive. No sucuri.

Per SKILL.md priority order, customer-visible Store API count wins. Live probe: x-wp-total=356 on /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products (default stock_status=instock). wp/v2/product reports 971 total (DB had stale 965; current is 971). The 615 admin-only delta = out-of-stock products. PROOF: 356 (instock) + 615 (outofstock via ?stock_status=outofstock) = 971 (wp/v2 total). Walked both APIs end-to-end, deduped by id, confirmed every wc/store id is in wp/v2 AND every wp/v2 id is fetchable individually via wc/store (it is the LIST endpoint that hides out-of-stock per WooCommerce's 'Hide out of stock items from the catalog' setting, not the single-product endpoint). Sample admin-only IDs (53130, 53127, 52921) all have class_list containing 'outofstock'; comparison product 53271 (in store list) has 'instock'. Coverage gate at backend/src/services/product-count-probe.ts uses this number as the divisor for bootstrap completion (95% threshold) — using 971 (admin) would force the crawler to find out-of-stock products it can never see via the catalog HTML, which is wrong. 356 is the operationally correct denominator.

DB value is WRONG. Read backend/src/services/catalog-crawler.ts:121-125: buildPaginatedUrl with type=path strips the trailing slash from baseUrl, then concatenates the template literally. DB template 'page/{N}/' would produce 'https://leverarms.com/product-category/gunspage/2/' (no slash between 'guns' and 'page') — verified 404. R1 template '/page/{N}/' produces 'https://leverarms.com/product-category/guns/page/2/' — verified 200. The leading slash is REQUIRED. DB row predates a fix to buildPaginatedUrl or was hand-edited.

RUNTIME CODE CHECK: grep across backend/src for 'apiEndpoints', 'productDiscovery', 'priceEnrichment', 'crawlers.bootstrap' returns ZERO matches. This field is documentation/audit-trail only — NOT consumed by any runtime adapter or scheduler. The WooCommerce bootstrap path is hardcoded in scraper/adapters/woocommerce.ts to /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products; it does not look this field up. Therefore the 2-step shape claimed in the R1 diff is FICTIONAL — there is no '2-step bootstrap cascade'. The DB's 'productDiscovery + priceEnrichment' naming is an operator-applied label with no runtime effect. R1's 'products + categories' naming is equally valid and matches the SKILL.md example shape. Neither value will affect crawler behavior. Recommend R1's flatter naming as the convention (matches the SKILL.md example output).
